references.text: The preceding verse that introduces the prohibition against harvesting in the sabbatical year and provides context for verse 5.
The Jubilee Year has similar rules about not harvesting what grows on its own or gathering grapes from unpruned vines.
Rules about leaving some of the harvest in the field, showing God's care for the poor and the foreigner.
The basic law of the sabbatical year in Exodus 2, where the land must rest every seventh year and the poor may eat what grows there.
Similar provisions to leave grapes and grain behind for the poor and the foreigner at harvest time.
The regulations of the sabbatical year extended to include the release of debts, showing the holy character of the seventh year.
A historical example that what grows on its own (ספיח) is eaten in times of need, linking to the self-sown crop of the sabbatical year.
Isaiah also mentions what grows on its own (ספיח) as a sign of the Lord's care in difficult times.
